slides.title: The Mixing Tower
slides.text: The first tower smells of lamp oil. Every lantern in Netville was mixed here, and each glow has its own recipe. The Jumble has muddled the recipes, so no two lanterns match. Tally hands you two dials.

slides.title: A ratio compares two amounts
slides.text: The gate lantern is mixed from 2 parts amber oil for every 3 parts blue oil. That comparison is a ratio, written 2 : 3. Order matters: 3 : 2 would be a different, more amber glow.

visual.label: A tape diagram of the gate glow: 2 equal parts of amber oil over 3 equal parts of blue oil

focus.cue: 2 parts of amber oil. Every part is the same size.
3 parts of blue oil go with them: the ratio is 2 : 3.

slides.title: Equal ratios, same glow
slides.text: Multiply both parts by the same number and the mix stays the same: 4 : 6 glows exactly like 2 : 3. Adding the same amount to both parts does not work. 3 : 4 is a new glow, with more amber in it.

visual.label: A double number line of equal ratios: 2 parts amber with 3 parts blue, then 4 with 6, 6 with 9 and 8 with 12

focus.cue: One batch of the glow: 2 parts amber with 3 parts blue.
Both parts doubled: 4 and 6. The same glow, twice as much.

slides.title: Fill a lantern of 15 parts
slides.text: A big lantern holds 15 parts and needs the 2 : 3 glow. One batch of 2 and 3 makes 5 parts. Build a ratio table, one more batch in each row, until the total reaches 15.

visual.label: A ratio table for the 2 : 3 glow: 2, 3 and 5 parts in all; 4, 6 and 10; 6, 9 and 15
head: Amber
Blue
Total

focus.cue: One batch: 2 parts amber, 3 parts blue, 5 parts in all.
Three batches reach 15 parts: 6 amber and 9 blue.

slides.title: Which glow has more amber?
slides.text: To compare two mixes, give them the same total. In 10 parts, the 2 : 3 glow has 4 parts amber. A mix of 5 and 5 has more amber in the same 10 parts, so it glows more amber.

visual.label: Two mixes of 10 parts each: 4 amber with 6 blue, and 5 amber with 5 blue

rows.label: The 2 : 3 glow in 10 parts: 4 amber, 6 blue
A 1 : 1 glow in 10 parts: 5 amber, 5 blue

focus.cue: The 2 : 3 glow, doubled to 10 parts: 4 are amber.
This mix has 5 amber parts in 10: more amber.

slides.title: Words to know
slides.text: Four words for mixing by ratio.

words.means: a comparison of two amounts, such as 2 parts amber for every 3 parts blue
ratios that describe the same mix, such as 2 : 3 and 4 : 6
rows of equivalent ratios, each made by multiplying both parts by one number
a bar cut into equal parts that shows the parts of a ratio

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Lantern Mix at Match the Glow. Set the two dials, light the lantern and match the gate glow. Six lanterns finish the step.
slides.alt: Lantern Mix on a phone: the gate lantern's gauge of 2 amber and 3 blue parts on the board, and two dials to set.
